messages.subject: UTF-8 characters in RApache
parts:
I am experiencing a problem in RApache when using UTF-characters. The problem does not appear in R on the same machine, it happens only when R is invoked through RApache. I am getting it both when escaping and not escaping the UTF. E.g:

cat("Z\303\274rich");
cat("\n");
cat("Zürich");

This script runs fine in R, but then when this is called through RApache the characters are messed up.

The same happens for plots. To reproduce:

setContentType(type='image/png')
t <- tempfile();
png(t);
plot(0, xlab="Zürich", ylab="Z\303\274rich")
dev.off()
sendBin(object=readBin(t,'raw',n=file.info(t)$size))

The same plot renders fine in R but not in RApache. Note that I am not using any funky locales:

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.14.1 (2011-12-22)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:
 [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C              
 [3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8        LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8    
 [5] LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8    LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8   
 [7] LC_PAPER=C                 LC_NAME=C                 
 [9] LC_ADDRESS=C               LC_TELEPHONE=C            
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: UTF-8 characters in RApache
parts:
You'll want to either set the locale before starting apache, however
on debian based systems (including Ubuntu) the startup scripts seem to
set the locale to C.

Otherwise, you can call Sys.setlocale() to the appropriate UTF locale.

For instance, this works on (most all?) ubuntu systems:

Sys.setlocale(category='LC_ALL','en_US.UTF-8')

Jeff
